prompt.context: You are a consultant. The senior partner wants you to manage a team of four other consultants to address the following client problem: your client is VP of Customer Service and her objectives are to decrease costs, increase revenues, and improve customer retention.
prompt.question: How would you approach this problem and how would you organize your team?

clarifying_info.q: Do you want me to address team issues or problem approach first?
What types of telecommunications services or products does the client offer?
clarifying_info.a: Long-distance, some local and wireless; the client also plans to enter the Internet market.

clarifying_info.q: Can I select or recruit my team?
clarifying_info.a: No. Your team has already been selected for you.

framework: Problem Approach: gather baseline data from the VP on profitability, revenues, cost drivers, and customer retention trends over recent years
Problem Approach: conduct industry and competitive benchmarking on the same dimensions to generate hypotheses
Problem Approach: investigate customer-service-specific root causes — survey churned customers (focus groups, phone surveys) and survey current customers on what they value most
Problem Approach: build a relative importance-performance matrix to identify quick-hit improvement areas
Problem Approach: identify feedback-loop breakdowns between Customer Service and other functions (e.g., sales not receiving timely product info from marketing)
Problem Approach: evaluate IT/systems integration opportunities to streamline key processes and reduce costs
Team Organization: assess team members' skill sets, experience, backgrounds, and individual preferences
Team Organization: match skill sets and preferences to work streams aligned with the three objectives (cost, revenue, retention)
Team Organization: forge consultant-client team relationship; establish cross-linkages, a joint work plan, key deliverables, and deadlines

questions.prompt: What initial information would you gather from the VP of Customer Service before forming hypotheses?
questions.guidance: Strong answers mention: multi-year trends for profitability, revenue, cost drivers, and customer retention rates; identification of key client contacts and subject-matter experts who will partner with the consulting team.

questions.prompt: How would you determine why customers are leaving?
questions.guidance: Organize focus groups and/or telephone surveys with recently churned customers to identify the key performance issues that caused them to leave. Complement with surveys of existing customers to learn what they value most in customer service.

questions.prompt: How would you prioritize which customer service issues to fix first?
questions.guidance: Build a relative importance-performance matrix: plot criteria by customer-weighted importance (high to low) and by current firm performance (low to high). Prioritize criteria that are highly important to customers AND where the firm currently performs poorly — these are the 'quick hits' with the greatest impact.

questions.prompt: How would you organize a team of four consultants for this engagement?
questions.guidance: (1) Identify each team member's skill sets, experience, and preferences. (2) Divide work streams around the three client objectives: cost reduction, revenue growth, and customer retention. (3) Assign people to work streams based on best fit between skills, preferences, and tasks. (4) Align the consultant team with client-side counterparts; establish cross-linkages, a joint work plan, deliverables, and deadlines.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the main customer service problems and feedback-loop breakdowns that could exist between Customer Service and other parts of the firm?

categories.name: Sales & Marketing alignment
ideas: Sales reps not receiving timely information on new product offerings
Lack of communication channel between sales and marketing on promotions
Customer-facing teams unaware of billing changes communicated only internally

categories.name: IT & Systems
ideas: Siloed customer databases prevent a single view of the customer
Manual processes that could be automated (order entry, complaint logging)
Lack of CRM integration causing duplicate contacts or lost follow-ups

categories.name: Operations & Billing
ideas: Billing errors leading to customer calls and churn
Slow resolution times due to handoff delays between departments
No escalation path for high-value customers

categories.name: People & Training
ideas: Inconsistent service quality due to gaps in agent training
No clear performance metrics or incentives tied to retention

recommendation: Identify the high-impact drivers of revenues, costs, and customer retention through benchmarking and customer research
Develop targeted strategies to improve performance on those key drivers, starting with quick-hit criteria that are highly important to customers and where current performance is lowest
Dedicate significant effort to team effectiveness through careful planning, clear role assignments, joint work plan with the client team, and disciplined communication and delivery
risks: Client team may resist external consultants' recommendations if relationship-building is neglected
Quick wins may be prioritized at the expense of longer-term systemic fixes (e.g., IT integration)
Internet market entry ambitions may distract focus from core customer service stabilization
next_steps: Schedule kick-off meeting with VP and key client stakeholders to align on scope and success metrics
Conduct churned-customer and current-customer surveys within first two weeks
Produce importance-performance matrix and present initial hypotheses to the senior partner and client within the first month
